title: [Cyrillisch:] Sleutel tot de geheimen van de natuur
shelf_note: A Russian pre-reform (ѣ, ъ, і) early-19th-century printing of Eckartshausen; the page is moral-philosophical/esoteric prose consistent with the author. The catalogue title is an odd Dutch cataloguer's form ('[Cyrillisch:] Sleutel tot…') but describes the work.
structure_note: 15 duplicate records (433 records vs 418 distinct page numbers) and 25 printed repeats suggest duplicated records or re-scanned leaves rather than misread numerals alone. structure.pages_translated is 0 while the book field says 401 translated, and this page does carry a translation, so the count looks wrong (E2). The record number 376 against printed 338 is a plausible front-matter offset.

pages.layout: single column, page number centred at head, section heading in spaced capitals, handwritten 'P' in left margin; fore-edge of the book block fills the left third and the scan cuts off the right edge of the text block

ocr_errors.image: a large handwritten ink 'P' in the left margin, a later reader's mark, not printed text
ocr_errors.problem: a later hand transcribed as page content (O13) and carried into the English

ocr_errors.problem: on every line the OCR supplies the last 1–3 letters, which the image does not show. The supplied letters are plausible, but they cannot be checked against this scan

tr_errors.problem: there is no vocabulary list on the printed page. The <vocab> tag is the OCR model's own keyword list, and the note presents it to the reader as part of the source

book_verdict: The text and translation on this page are sound and faithful. The page's problems are a scan that cuts off the line ends, a reader's ink 'P' carried in as text, and a note that wrongly claims a vocabulary list is printed on the page. The structure counts point to duplicate records and a wrong translated-page count.
